ashrae621_2022.new_text: STANDARD (US, benchmark; J.B. upload 1 Nov 2026): ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 62.1-2022, Ventilation and Acceptable Indoor Air Quality: 5.4.1 outdoor air intakes (incl. natural-ventilation openings) at least the Table 5-1 distance from each source, or per Normative Appendix B; Table 5-1 (p. 10): Class 2 exhaust/relief outlet 3 m; Class 3 5 m; Class 4 10 m; evaporative heat-rejection (cooling tower) exhaust 7.5 m, intake or basin 5 m; driveway, street or parking 1.5 m; garage entry or loading area 5 m; garbage or dumpsters 5 m; thoroughfare with high traffic 7.5 m; truck loading area or dock, bus parking/idling 7.5 m; vents, chimneys and flues from combustion appliances and equipment 5 m; surface below intake 0.3 m; 5.4.1.2 fuel-burning equipment distances follow NFPA 54, NFPA 31, NFPA 211 (not read ?); Appendix B (p. 40–41): B1 applies to operable windows, skylights and doors on the subject property and on adjacent properties alike; B1.3 Class 3, Class 4, cooling-tower and combustion exhaust must be the full distance L from operable openings to occupiable spaces (other exhaust half L); B1.4 no credit for vertical separation where exhaust is less than 20 m below an intake or window; B1.6 exhaust to property line half L, except Class 3/4 or combustion exhaust at least 3 m above grade beside a public way; Table B-1 Class 3 5 m, Class 4 10 m; 6.1.4.2 outdoor air filtered to MERV 11 or better where PM2.5 exceeds the national standard. The 2022 edition has no generator-specific row (the diesel-generator dilution factor is in a later addendum, see arch_ashrae621ag); this edition's combustion-flue row (5 m) is our closest reading for generator exhaust (?). ‖ CHECK 2 (1 Nov 2026, fixed): all figures confirmed; adjacent-property phrase moved to B1 (general), where it sits
